title: Video Gaming Activates Pleasure Centers
content: A studybySimone Kuhn of Ghent, Belgiumsuggests that playing video games changes the brain and activates the same pleasure centers that light up when gambling. Even when losing, a player is hooked by the payoffs of hormones and deep neural centers.But I think that puts video games in an unfair light. I'll bet that a lot of the things we love to do, such as sketching, probably activate the same "reward hub." For me, laying in a watercolor wash feels like pulling a slot machine handle. More times than not, I lose my quarter and come up empty. But something in my brain says, "Pull the handle one more time!"---------BBC article about the studyOriginal article cited in NatureGraphic adapted from CRN blog
